text:
maya (support): FYI — multiple customers opened tickets this morning after the rate-limit policy change we promoted to Canary A. getting lots of 429s and aborted streaming. ticket examples: #3452, #3454. can we triage? :eyes:

simon (eng-sre): which canary exactly? the push from last night?

maya (support): yes, the policy that lowered burst window for API keys on the hosted tier (canary-id: canary-A-2026-03-15). traffic spike around 09:12 PST. observability shows 429 spike in us-west-2 region.

jess (eng-platform): looking at dashboards — overall qps steady, but per-key short bursts exceed the new per-key bucket size. Canary A was configured with: `rate: 300r/m`, `burst: 50` -> reduced from previous `burst: 200`.

simon (eng-sre): that burst drop could cause tail errors for customers that do short fanout calls. do we have request examples? maya can you paste a repro?

maya (support): customer repro (anonymized):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-lite","input":"predictive step","max_tokens":64}'
```
They see: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` and streaming abort message: `stream aborted: rate_limit_exceeded`.

arnold (oncall): I'm seeing identical 429 traces in the request logs for the canary pool: 09:11:30 -> 09:14:00 window. Breakdown by API key shows several keys hit burst limit then fall back to 429s. attaching a log snippet:
```
[09:12:01] key=acct-prod-123 total_req=68 window=60 burst_remaining=0 -> 429
[09:12:03] key=acct-prod-456 total_req=55 window=60 burst_remaining=0 -> 429
[09:12:05] key=acct-prod-123 stream_abort reason=rate_limit_exceeded
```

simon (eng-sre): thanks. initial hypothesis: our staged policy is too aggressive on burst for some high-fanout customers. Canary traffic probably includes small groups of real customers that exercise bursts. Two options: 1) roll the canary back to previous burst size; 2) patch policy to be more permissive (increase burst or add short-term grace). Which is faster?

jess (eng-platform): rollback is fastest. we can revert the canary policy config via the control-plane and re-evaluate. patching and re-releasing still needs canary validation.

maya (support): customers are getting degraded UX. recommend rollback. any risk to rollback?

simon (eng-sre): low risk — this was a policy change in control plane only, no infra change. rollback will restore previous `burst:200` for canary group. we need to coordinate with deploy-bot to apply rollback and monitor for resolution and error rate drop.

arnold (oncall): I'm on it. initiating rollback now. @deploy-bot please execute `policy rollback canary-A` and confirm.

deploy-bot: executing command...
`/redwoodctl policy rollback --canary canary-A-2026-03-15`

deploy-bot: rollback started. applying previous config (burst:200). rolling back in 3 stages across nodes. progress: 0% -> 30%

simon (eng-sre): while rollback runs, let's add quick mitigation (throttle control) — increase per-key burst limit in the canary region only so we don't widen blast radius elsewhere. also add temporary auto-throttle fallback to queue requests instead of immediate 429 for streaming flows.

deploy-bot: progress update: 30% -> 75% -> 100%. rollback complete.

arnold (oncall): rollback applied at 09:18 PST. observing metrics now. error rate dropping in us-west-2.

maya (support): customer #3452 confirmed recovery at 09:20 and streams resumed.

jess (eng-platform): nice. action items: 1) revert canary config change and hold on policy until we test with synthetic workloads that emulate fanout patterns; 2) add synthetic test to CI that runs small bursty fanout against canary; 3) consider graduated burst reduction (e.g., ramp from 200->150->100) instead of one-step.

simon (eng-sre): addendum: we should also update rollout playbook to require a 24-hour targeted traffic simulation before changing burst settings for hosted keys.

arnold (oncall): logging note: we recorded the incident as S2 (customer-facing but mitigated quickly). I'll open the postmortem stub and assign owners.

maya (support): I'll reply to the customers with timeline and note that we rolled back the canary and will follow up with permanent plan.

jess (eng-platform): follow-up PR to change canary process and add tests: #pl-512. tagging @simon for review.

simon (eng-sre): ack. will review. final note: if we re-rollout, shrink burst in smaller increments and send warning to higher-fanout customers so they can adjust.

deploy-bot: incident resolved marker added to canary-A-2026-03-15: status=rolled-back, initiated_by=arnold, completed=1802504385

maya (support): thanks team. closing the immediate ticket cluster, leaving follow-up items in #postmortems. :thumbsup:
